I think goats are pretty cool. I want to get one to act as a pet, and to nom on the grasses on my property. But I'm not an idiot, goats are animals, they need care, and have conditions they prefer, And I dont want to milk a goat so females are out. SO uhhh... How does one care for a goat? Can they really eat anything? What kind of upkeep costs are we looking at?
How difficult is it to care for a goat?

Context: use to work at a 4-H. We had goats.

It depends where you live.

If you live in, or within ~30 miles of, a community with a lot of small farmers, it will be much less difficult.

You probably won't, so let me pose a few sobering, easily possible points about the cost of raising a goat.

  • You know how if a dog eats something and its digestive system can't handle it, the dog can die if you don't take it to the vet and pay for thousand+ dollar surgery, and the same for a host of dozens of the more serious dog diseases and health problems? Okay, now imagine that for an animal three times the size, and you need a specialist who is rare and has to come to you, or you have to bring the goat to them. Goaty gets sick the wrong way. That's it, your goat is dead, unless you live near a farming community or have $3000 minimum you could drop at a moments notice with no difficulty. At a certain point, it becomes a lot cheaper to just get a new goat, and when you get to the point you're asking those tough questions you have to confront that getting a goat is an emotional commitment on the level of dog or more.

  • Adult goats require space to be happy and to live off the land. Lots of space. If you don't live on great grazing land, you're going to need at least a third of an acre per goat. That's a little less than a third of a football field. If you are willing to buy feed, you could still keep a goat basically satisfied on a sixth of an acre, but that's probably still more land than you have if you live in the suburbs.

  • It gets cold in the winter. How are you going to keep your goat from dying in your fenced in, wind-susceptible probably-flatland pasture during the winter.

  • Coyotes love goats

OK, you say you don't want a female goat, but uncastrated male goats make very very bad pets for a number of reasons. (Smelly, aggressive, horny) A female can be an excellent pet but they are herd animals and generally prefer companionship of their own kind. They do require a lot of space to be happy, though, and they are naturally predisposed to browsing rather than grazing (meaning they prefer to reach up for their food, rather than down - they prefer bushes, shrubs etc to grass on the ground and teaching them to graze usually involves penning them with sheep who are more naturally inclined to graze and will rub off on the goats given time.) That said, to keep a goat fed properly you will probably want to supply them with alfalfa hay. Other forms of hay may not be nutritious enough for them, though it matters a little less if you aren't milking them. For an occasional treat, they enjoy rolled corn or barley-corn mix in small (1 c a day or so) amounts, even more so if it's dry cob (feedstores will generally know what this is). Keep the barrel with the dry cob or rolled corn secure though, as if they get into it they can make themselves very sick. The myth that they can eat anything stems from their tendency to try to taste everything. They're kind of like babies, they test things with their mouth a lot. There are many useful guides to caring for and raising goats of many breeds, from "meat breeds" like Boers, to "dairy breeds" like Alpines, Nubians and Lamanchas, and "pet breeds" like Pygmies. A quick search on Amazon yielded lots of results, and chances are good you could find a good book on the matter at your local library. Read up on them well before you make the leap to getting a goat (or a pair, as the case may be), and remember forewarned is forearmed - goats are clever and mischievous animals, and you really have to outthink them sometimes.

Denial can be one hell of a thing here. The person really has to want to. My gf has threatened to leave me if I started drinking again. When she did find out I had relapsed, did she leave me?
